newsitem.title: UK: Metals buckle on LME, markets end easier.
newsitem.headline: Metals buckle on LME, markets end easier.

text.p: Base metal prices continued to trend lower during Friday afternoon LME trading, as confirmation of bearish chart signals prompted general liquidation, traders said.
All the markets finished in the minus column, and further losses will likely be sustained next week as investment funds are sucked in to add to existing short positions.
Charts have all turned negative in recent sessions, and Friday's closes are similarly technically unimpressive with all markets near their lows, traders added.

Copper was unable to hold on to $2,300, and after some desultory business in the official rings, a lower New York trend sent prices under important chart support at $2,280. The backwardation also narrowed from above $40 to around $38, basis cash/threes.
Last business was at $2,269 a tonne, down $33 from Thursday's kerb close.
Aluminium similarly fell away, underlining persistent failures at or near $1,600 recently, and by the close of the kerb prices were $22 easier at $1,564 and seen heading for $1,550.
Nickel prices remained above their lows during the afternoon, although bearish charts continued to weigh on the market. The market closed at $7,250, down $25.
Lead continued to trade near early 18-month lows of $625, concluding $12 easier at $627, with fundamentals giving scant support.
Physicals are slow at present, and the unseasonably mild weather in Northern Europe does not bode well for battery manufacturer offtake, they said.
Zinc drifted lower with the main trend, ending at $1,232, a loss of $12. However, the fundamental picture is fairly constructive, which should restrict further declines.
Tin eased to $5,630, down $60, while alloy was marked down to $1,455/60 a tonne, a loss of $15. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
